cards.explanation: The answer is His own flesh and blood. All the tribes of Israel come to David at Hebron and say, “Here we are, your own flesh and blood.” (2 Samuel 5:1) They're basically saying, "We're family, we belong together." I think that's a mighty warm way to walk into a room, friends.
The answer is David. The tribes tell him, “…you were the one who led Israel out and brought them back.” (2 Samuel 5:2) And they say it about the days while Saul was still king, friends.

The answer is shepherd them. The tribes quote the LORD saying to David, “You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over them.” (2 Samuel 5:2) Shepherd AND ruler, both in one sentence, bakers.

The answer is False. Here's what the text really says: David makes a covenant with the elders before the LORD, and they anoint him king over Israel. (2 Samuel 5:3) No army commander job shows up in that verse, friends. They're giving him something bigger than a title on a uniform.

The answer is thirty-three years. In Jerusalem David reigns “…thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.” (2 Samuel 5:5) Hebron's seven years and six months come first, and the verse before it gives his forty years as the whole reign. (2 Samuel 5:4)

The answer is True. The Jebusites say to David, “You will never get in here. Even the blind and lame can repel you.” (2 Samuel 5:6) That's some big talk to say to a man marching at your gate, friends. Remember it, because it's about to matter.

The answer is True. The Jebusites were sure, but the text says, “Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion (that is, the City of David).” (2 Samuel 5:7) "Nevertheless" is a great word, bakers. It means all that confidence didn't change a thing.

The answer is that he builds it up all the way around. David takes up residence in the fortress, calls it the City of David, and builds it up “…all the way around, from the supporting terraces inward.” (2 Samuel 5:9) He's not just visiting, friends. He moves in and gets to work.

The answer is that the LORD God of Hosts is with him. The text says, “…David became greater and greater, for the LORD God of Hosts was with him.” (2 Samuel 5:10) The reason is right there in the verse, bakers. The LORD being with him is the whole story.

The answer is palace. Hiram, king of Tyre, sends envoys, cedar logs, carpenters and stonemasons, “…and they built a palace for David.” (2 Samuel 5:11) That's a good use of cedar, friends. A whole crew and a pile of logs, all sent by the king of Tyre.

The answer is False. The text says David realized the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom “…for the sake of His people Israel.” (2 Samuel 5:12) So it's for the people, not for David's own sake. I think that's worth remembering about any kind of leading, friends.
